Who is actually paying for war in 2025?

This map shows military spending as a share of GDP — and one country is so far ahead it broke the color scale.

One data map, explained — a thread 🧵🗺️

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)

1/ The near-black country is Ukraine: roughly a THIRD of its entire economy goes to defense — a level unseen anywhere since WW2.

Russia, the huge dark red mass, is at ~7% and climbing: its highest burden since the Soviet collapse.

2/ For scale: at the peak of WW2 the US pushed ~40% of GDP into the war. Cold War America ran 6-9%.

Today the US spends ~3.4% — historically low for a superpower, yet still the largest military budget on Earth in absolute terms.

3/ Notice the second dark belt: Algeria, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Israel — the Middle East and North Africa spend more of their income on arms than almost anyone else, war or no war.

Oil money and rivalry keep the region permanently armed.

4/ Europe's shift is the quiet story. For decades most of NATO ignored its 2% guideline — Germany spent ~1.1% in 2005.

After 2022, nearly every member jumped past 2%, with Poland and the Baltics pushing toward 4-5%. The continent is rearming at Cold War pace.

5/ The long view: after 1990 the world cashed in a "peace dividend" — global military burden fell from ~4% of world GDP in the 1960s to near 2%.

That 30-year decline has now reversed. The 2020s are the first decade of sustained rearmament since the Cold War.

6/ Maps of borders show where wars happened. This one hints where the next ones might.
